key_insight: λ-MACE enables experimentally accurate hydration free energies for drug-like molecules, but combined hydration and sublimation errors still limit crystalline solubility predictions.
engineering_relevance: Physics-based solubility prediction could support drug formulation decisions, provided crystalline thermodynamics can be modeled more accurately.
method: Optimize λ-MACE for condensed-phase free energy calculations.
Compute hydration and sublimation free energies using MACE-driven calculations.
Combine both contributions to predict solubility from known experimental crystal structures.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered 70 medicinally relevant FreeSolv compounds for hydration and 10 additional compounds for crystalline solubility, yielding solubility accuracy of 1.53 log units versus experimental accuracy of 0.17–0.6 log units.
watch_item: Reaching experimental solubility accuracy requires roughly 0.5 kcal/mol accuracy in each free energy leg, with crystalline thermodynamics the hardest remaining challenge.
paper_title: Computing hydration free energies and crystalline solubility of drug-like molecules with MACE
